--- title: "Time aggregation" --- The paper's second result is what goes wrong when an econometrician ignores time aggregation. Forcing $h = 1$ says the agent decides once a year, the sampling interval of the data. The persistent growth shock then looks like short-run noise, risk aversion is inflated, and the model is rejected. This page holds Tables 4 to 6 and Figure 2. The market fit itself is on [Estimation](estimation.qmd). ::: {#b51ec741 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"} from great_tables import GT from geap.lrr.estimation import ( TABLE_5_ANNUAL_MODEL, TABLE_5_ANNUAL_RESIDUALS, estimate_bky, figure2_ggplot, figure2_irf, load_annual, long_run_variance_share, table3_compare, table4_annual_on_lrr_sims, table4_frame, table6_frame, ) KIKU_GT = dict(table_background_color="transparent", table_font_size="0.92rem", heading_title_font_size="1.05rem", heading_subtitle_font_size="0.85rem", source_notes_font_size="0.8rem", column_labels_font_weight="bold", data_row_padding="4px") def fmt_params(gt, tab): """Two decimals for the large parameters, four for the rest, scientific for sigma_w.""" idx = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(tab["parameter"])} two = [idx[n] for n in ("gamma", "psi", "phi_d", "phi_d_sigma", "h", "J") if n in idx] three = [idx[n] for n in ("rho_d", "p") if n in idx] sci = [idx[n] for n in ("sigma_w",) if n in idx] four = [i for i in range(len(tab)) if i not in two + three + sci] num = [c for c in tab.columns if c != "parameter"] return ( gt.fmt_number(columns=num, rows=four, decimals=4) .fmt_number(columns=num, rows=two, decimals=2) .fmt_number(columns=num, rows=three, decimals=3) .fmt_scientific(columns=num, rows=sci, decimals=2) .sub_missing(missing_text="") ) def fmt_moments(gt, tab): idx = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(tab["moment"])} sci = [idx[n] for n in ("e_eta_x", "e_eta2_s2") if n in idx] rest = [i for i in range(len(tab)) if i not in sci] num = [c for c in tab.columns if c != "moment"] levels = [c for c in num if not c.startswith("t_diff")] tstats = [c for c in num if c.startswith("t_diff")] gt = gt.fmt_number(columns=num, rows=rest, decimals=3) gt = gt.fmt_scientific(columns=levels, rows=sci, decimals=1) if tstats: gt = gt.fmt_number(columns=tstats, rows=sci, decimals=3) return gt.sub_missing(missing_text="") panel = load_annual() ``` ::: ## Table 4: the annual specification The CUE surface at $h = 1$ has several local minima. The fit below is the lowest objective of six generic starts that differ in the IES and in how consumption risk splits between the persistent and the short-run shock. The simulated columns re-estimate the annual specification on samples drawn from an LRR economy. The paper draws from its Table 2 estimates; we draw from the monthly fixed-frequency fit of Table 6 on this page, twenty samples of 86 years, and fit each with the same CUE as the empirical column from a single start. ::: {#bf42e515 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ann = estimate_bky(panel, h=1, n_starts=6) fits = {h: estimate_bky(panel, h=h, n_starts=3) for h in (26, 12, 4)} fits[1] = ann mc = table4_annual_on_lrr_sims( n_draws=20, years=86, seed=0, lrr_params=fits[12].params, lrr_h=12 ) tab4 = table4_frame(ann, mc) empirical = tab4[["parameter", "hat", "se_hat", "paper", "se_paper"]] fmt_params( GT(empirical) .tab_header(title="Table 4, empirical data. Annual specification, h = 1") .cols_label(parameter="", hat="estimate", se_hat="SE", paper="paper", se_paper="paper SE") .tab_source_note("Paper: BKY (2016) Table 4, first two columns."), empirical, ).tab_options(**KIKU_GT) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

Everything else is computed by the cell above it. Our $J$ statistics reject the annual and quarterly specifications as the paper's do, but they are an order of magnitude smaller than the printed ones; the difference in the weighting and the covariance estimator is not resolved. The annual fit is the lowest of six generic starts; a start at the paper's printed Table 4 vector reaches a lower objective still, with persistence 0.87 and a larger short-run loading, so the surface has basins our starts do not reach. The simulated columns of Table 4 rest on 20 draws, each fitted from one start. `NUMBERS.md` lists the open caveats. :::
